pos.personaBrief: La Máquina aimed at possession with short passes (La Página Millonaria, Juvenal 1943 seven-pass goal), though Cesarini's stated view prizes winning over beauty.

pro.personaBrief: River built from the back with short passes and inside-forwards dropping to link (Juvenal 1942, La Página Millonaria), not a direct side; Muñoz said they did not rush for goal.

est.personaBrief: Forwards swapped positions and Pedernera dropped from the 9 role (Juvenal 1942, Wilson), and Cesarini ran free 'fútbol loco' sessions; yet he sent wingers to the touchline.

lar.personaBrief: Two true wingers in the front five (Muñoz, Deambrosi, then Loustau moved to the left wing by Cesarini), and his 1965 view: widen the pitch and send the punteros to the line.

blo.personaBrief: Little verified on pressing or block height; a possession side that outpassed opponents and did not sit deep, so answers rely on general inference and are mild.

mar.personaBrief: Only individual marking is verified (Yácono the 'stamp', specialist man-marker); the 1940s W-M norm was man-oriented, so team marking is inferred from general knowledge.

pla.personaBrief: No verified evidence on this axis, so these answers come from general knowledge of Cesarini: a coach who imposes his principles and keeps River's style (1965: 'yo impongo los principios'), consistent with the verified evidence.

res.personaBrief: His 1965 statements say the only truth is winning ('basta de bordados'); I weigh that heavily, though La Máquina was admired as a spectacle.

sis.personaBrief: He gave stars freedom (fútbol loco, Pedernera choosing the 9 role) but demands sacrifice and function from all; he builds players and imposes principles.

jog.personaBrief: Stated view: physique, stamina, speed and sacrifice first, skill without physique is of no use (1965); the River side was technical, but his criteria lean physical.

bas.personaBrief: He backed the young free Loustau over a purchase and took Muñoz and Yácono-type youngsters into a title side; says anyone can play, divisions should share one style, but pays less attention to academy primacy.

lid.personaBrief: Known for authority on all matters (Wikipedia, 'La Biblia del fútbol'); 1965: assistants must agree or leave, 'yo impongo los principios'; he watched silently in training but decided alone.
